zh.title: 瑞典再撥款薩博300億美元測試戰後機技術
zh.summary: 瑞典再撥款薩博300億美元測試未來戰機技術
body: 瑞典已授予薩博（Saab）額外29億瑞典克朗（約3億美元），用於開發及示範其未來作戰空中系統的技術。
該訂單由瑞典國防物資管理局（FMV）發出，涵蓋2026至2028年的工作，並可選擇延續至2029及2030年，包括飛行與地面示範機、先進研究，以及涵蓋有人及無人戰機的概念開發。
薩博將於系統整合、自主性、推進、訊號管理、數位開發及未來生產方法上進行工作，目的是測試技術、降低技術風險，並在瑞典決定最終由何種機型接替或與獅鷲（Gripen）並肩作戰時提供更多選項。
這是薩博在該計畫下第二次獲得資金。2025年10月，FMV授予薩博另外26億瑞典克朗，用於概念研究、技術開發及示範機，直至2027年。

en.title: Sweden awards Saab additional $300m to test post-Gripen fighter technologies
en.summary: Sweden commits SEK 2.9bn for Saab to develop and demonstrate future combat air system technologies.
body: Sweden has awarded Saab a further SEK 2.9 billion (approximately $300 million) to develop and demonstrate technologies for its future combat air system.

The order from the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration (FMV) covers work between 2026 and 2028, with options to continue during 2029 and 2030. It includes flying and ground-based demonstrators, advanced studies and the development of concepts spanning crewed and uncrewed aircraft.

Saab will work on systems integration, autonomy, propulsion, signature management, digital development and future production methods. The purpose is to test technologies, reduce technical risk and give Sweden more options when it decides what should eventually succeed or operate alongside the Gripen.

This is not the first funding Saab has received under the programme. In October 2025, FMV awarded Saab a further SEK 2.6 billion, then worth around $270 million, for concept studies, technology development and demonstrators through 2027.

zh.title: 英國NATS故障後逾1300航班取消 業者加開班次疏運
zh.summary: NATS故障致逾1300航班取消；英航、易捷等加開班次疏運
body: 英國空中交通管制服務商NATS日前因技術問題導致航班處理系統故障，系統已恢復運作，但影響仍在。據FlightRadar24統計，週二英國全國有超過1300個航班取消，截至週三上午又增加177個取消。
英國航空、易捷航空、瑞安航空、Jet2及威茲航空等業者正在處理積壓，國際航空如荷蘭皇家航空、漢莎航空及瑞士航空也受到影響。英國航空表示已徹夜調整班表，盡量營運，但因飛機與組員位置錯亂，被迫取消原班表逾190班。
當前並無統一的「救援航班」名單，各家航空透過恢復取消的航班、增開臨時航班、更換航機調度及將旅客改簽至現有航班等方式紓解。希斯洛、蓋特威克、史坦斯特、盧頓、曼徹斯特及伯明罕等主要機場都在進行恢復作業，倫敦城市機場則表示運作已恢復正常。

en.title: NATS outage: Over 1,300 flights cancelled Tuesday; airlines add extra services to clear backlog
en.summary: NATS outage: 1,300+ flights cancelled; airlines add services to rebook stranded passengers
body: The UK's air traffic control system has resumed operations after Tuesday's NATS failure, but disruption continues. According to FlightRadar data, over 1,300 flights were cancelled across the UK on Tuesday, with a further 177 cancellations recorded by Wednesday morning.

British Airways, easyJet, Ryanair, Jet2 and Wizz Air are among carriers working through the backlog, while international airlines including KLM, Lufthansa and SWISS are also affected. British Airways said it worked overnight to create a revised schedule and operate as many flights as possible, but had to cancel more than 190 flights from its original schedule.

There is no central network of rescue flights; airlines are reinstating cancelled services, adding ad hoc flights, changing aircraft rotations and rebooking passengers onto existing departures. Recovery operations are ongoing at airports including Heathrow, Gatwick, Stansted, Luton, Manchester and Birmingham, while London City Airport says operations have returned to normal.
